chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a camel resists you and you intend to slaughter it, then it runs away from you — if you fear it will escape you, strike it with a sword or stab it with a spear, after invoking the Name (Bismillah). Then eat it. Except if you reach it while it has not yet died, then slaughter it (properly).

key_terms.تُسَمِّيَ: To pronounce the name of God (Bismillah) over the animal before slaughter, a required condition for permissibility
key_terms.ذَكِّهِ: From tadhkiya — the proper Islamic slaughter; to make the animal permissible (halal) through correct ritual slaughter
key_terms.نَحَرَ: To slaughter a camel by piercing the throat at the base of the neck (nahara), as opposed to dhabaha (cutting the throat) used for other animals

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a camel runs away before being slaughtered in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling from Imam al-Sadiq on the permissibility of consuming a camel that was struck down to prevent it escaping slaughter. The ruling distinguishes between two scenarios: if the animal dies from the blow (after Bismillah is invoked), the meat is permissible; if it is still alive when reached, a proper slaughter (tadhkiya) must be performed. This reflects the principle that the declaration of God's name and intent to slaughter are sufficient for permissibility even when conventional slaughter is impossible.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘When a camel is preventing you and you are intending to sacrifice it, so let it go away from you. So if you fear that it would precede you, so strike it with a sword, or stab it with a spear after you Name (Bismillah). So eat, except if you come to it and if it has not died afterwards, so slaughter it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Safwan from ‘Is ibn al-Qasim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once in al-Kufah a bull revolted and broke loose. People rushed with their swords and beat it down. They asked ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about it and he (the Imam) said, ‘It is a fast slaughtering but its flesh is lawful for food.’”
